purpose: Verify that SRM airport departure-capacity constraints actually change the recovered schedule and that the Workbench capacity/disruption representation is consistent with the formal solver.
interval_semantics: SRM counts an operated departure in interval [start_time,end_time) when start_time <= dep_time < end_time.

optimization_logic.explanation: In the bottleneck variant exactly two of four 09:00-10:00 departures must move out of the interval. Moving F101/F102/F103/F104 costs 60/50/40/30 respectively, so the unique minimum is to delay F103 and F104 for total schedule cost 70.

manual_checks: The baseline bundle has B departure capacity 4 in 09:00-10:00 and no disruption; all four original departures remain selected.
The bottleneck bundle changes B departure capacity in 09:00-10:00 from 4 to 2 and adds a matching departure_capacity_reduction disruption with capacity_change=-2.
Capacity Heatmap / Constraints should show the reduced B departure capacity in the bottleneck variant.
Solve Precheck is input readiness only and should report both complete bundles solve-ready.
The bottleneck recovered schedule has exactly two B departures in 09:00-10:00 and two at 10:05.
F103 and F104 are the delayed flights because their 40- and 30-minute shifts are the least expensive pair.
No passenger, aircraft-reassignment, crew-reassignment, ferry, or deadhead mechanism is needed.
design_notes: Four one-leg flights with four equipment/rating types are used despite exceeding the preferred 2-3 resource count because this gives the clearest 4-departures-versus-capacity-2 acceptance test without resource coupling.
No Cancel options are provided: the test is intentionally a pure capacity-driven retiming problem, and each flight has a feasible delayed operate option.
The matching disruption is included for Workbench visualization; the binding solver restriction is the airport interval dep_capacity in the bottleneck Scenario.
All delayed alternatives depart exactly at 10:05, safely outside the half-open [09:00,10:00) constrained interval and inside the next interval with capacity 4.
